:::{#thm-affine-map-unique}
#### An affine map determines its matrix and offset

If $f(\vx) = \matr{A}\vx + \vec{b}$ and $f(\vx) = \matr{A}'\vx + \vec{b}'$
for all $\vx \in \reals^p$ (@def-affine-map),
then $\matr{A}' = \matr{A}$ and $\vec{b}' = \vec{b}$.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-affine-map-zero, applied to each formula,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vec{b} &= f(\vzero) \\
&= \vec{b}'.
\end{aligned}
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{A}\vx &= f(\vx) - \vec{b} \\
&= \matr{A}'\vx
\end{aligned}
$$

for all $\vx$,
so $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{A}'$ are both matrices (@def-matrix-of-linear-map) of the linear map
$\vx \mapsto f(\vx) - \vec{b}$ (linear by @thm-matrix-map-linear),
and the uniqueness in @thm-linear-map-matrix gives $\matr{A}' = \matr{A}$.

:::
